maria: Heads-up — new sample app reported import errors when using our SDK in a Next.js edge function. Devs hit this on onboarding and it looks like the dual-package setup + conditional exports edge case is the culprit. :grimacing:

sam: ugh, which error? ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED or runtime 'require is not defined'?

maria: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED in local dev server, and in prod edge it throws 'Unexpected token export' from the CJS build. Repro steps in the sample repo: clone + yarn dev -> import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference' in middleware.ts (edge)

jia: can you paste the stack? Also which Node/browser runtime? Next edge uses V8 isolates (edge runtime) not Node, so CJS won't work there.

maria: pasted logs in the repo issue: 
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
 at file:///workspace/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs:1:1
```

tyler: that file path implies the bundler is resolving to dist/index.cjs for edge. Our conditional exports map probably points node -> ./dist/index.cjs and default -> ./dist/index.mjs but Next's resolver picks the wrong entry.

lucy: agreed. Also saw people confused by 'main' vs 'module' vs 'exports' + types. We need a clear playbook. Current package.json has: 
```
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./*": {
    "node": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "default": "./dist/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

sam: that exports layout is too coarse. For conditional exports you should export the package root and specific subpaths. For edge we want to expose an entry that points to the ESM build explicitly. e.g.: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./*": "./dist/*"
}
```

jia: +1 to separating dist/node and dist/edge builds. Also make sure to ship an index.cjs that re-exports the ESM default via dynamic import for compatibility? Might be hairy.

lucy: dynamic import shim for CJS is brittle for older Node versions. I'd rather keep explicit node CJS and edge ESM builds and a clear doc: "For edge environments import from '@redwood/inference/edge'" as an interim.

maria: users won't find that unless we update sample apps and onboarding docs. The sample app imported from "@redwood/inference" so it broke.

ops-bot: CI alert: publishing pipeline failed on canary smoke test for samples (test-suite #137). Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/137 :rotating_light:

tyler: ok proposal: 1) change exports to explicit import/require splits and add an "/edge" entry that points to ESM edge build. 2) update samples to import from '/edge' in edge functions. 3) add a build target that outputs dist/node and dist/edge and types at root. 4) add test that runs sample edge functions in V8 isolate runner.

sam: also add a migration note: if you import default from CJS via `const r = require('@redwood/inference')`, keep working. If you used ESM `import` in Node <14, document that they may need `experimental-modules` or migrate to Node 16+.

jia: we should update package.json types entry too. Right now "types" points to dist/index.d.ts but if we split builds we should point types to dist/types/index.d.ts and use "typesVersions" mapping for different import paths so TS resolves correctly. Example: 
```
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"typesVersions": {
  "*": {
    "edge": ["dist/types/edge/index.d.ts"],
    "*": ["dist/types/index.d.ts"]
  }
}
```

lucy: hm typesVersions is mostly for path imports. Might be simpler: keep single types surface that covers both builds (edge/node) since runtime differences don't affect types. One set of declarations under dist/index.d.ts is fine as long as we preserve exported API shape.

maria: action items I can take: update package.json exports to explicit import/require with "/edge" path, rearrange build script to emit dist/edge and dist/node, update sample app imports, and add CI smoke test. Who can own docs + migration note?

sam: I can draft the migration note + samples PR tomorrow. I'll also add a small note on using bundlers (webpack/rollup) — they sometimes treat conditional exports differently.

tyler: I'll add the smoke test to canary suite and wire a quick V8 runner job. ops-bot — can you mute the current CI alert once we have a new canary?

ops-bot: Will mute alert when canary #138 passes.

jia: one more thing — consider publishing a single ESM-first package and a compatibility CJS bundle under a subpath instead of dual main/module. Long term it's simpler and signals ESM-first. But that's a bigger breaking-change and needs RFC.

lucy: agree, add RFC to backlog. For now do the explicit export entries and docs so onboarding improves quickly. :thumbsup:

maria: cool — I'll open PRs: 1) build + package.json exports 2) samples update 3) docs/migration. Tagging @sam @tyler for review. Thanks everyone.

sam: thanks — appreciate the quick sync. :sparkles:
__notes: messages are concise, Slack-style, include code blocks, @mentions, and an ops bot line. No title per agents.md.
